formatNotes: First year of the revamped qualification system: every Open national champion, every Sanctional event winner, and the top 20 worldwide in the Open earned invitations, producing the largest individual fields in Games history (per Wikipedia 148 men and 134 women qualified; 143 men and 117 women started; the official leaderboard lists 144 men and 131 women including withdrawals). The huge field was trimmed with aggressive progressive cuts: to 75 athletes after Event 1, 50 after Event 2, 40 after Event 3, 30 after Event 4, 20 after Event 5, and 10 after Event 6, so only the final 10 per division contested Saturday night and Sunday. Event scoring tables were adjusted after the cuts so that later, smaller-field events created larger point differences than the early events. Events were contested across the Alliant Energy Center campus: the outdoor North Park stadium, the indoor Coliseum, the surrounding grounds (Ruck), and Lake Monona (Swim Paddle).
yearSummary: The 2019 Games tore up the format book: a field of well over a hundred per division, assembled from Open national champions and Sanctional winners, was cut roughly in half after the very first event and whittled to 10 by Saturday afternoon. The programming was correspondingly varied - a weighted ruck run and a zigzag sprint bracket debuted alongside a lake swim-paddle, the classic gymnastics benchmark Mary, a 1-rep-max clean ladder, and a finale (The Standard) that fused Grace and Isabel around 30 ring muscle-ups. Noah Ohlsen carried the lead through Friday night's Mary, but Mat Fraser seized it with back-to-back Saturday night wins in the Split Triplet and the Clean and never gave it back, winning four of the last six events to claim a record-tying fourth consecutive title. Tia-Clair Toomey won five of twelve events and cruised to a then-record 195-point margin, becoming the first woman to win three straight CrossFit Games. The cut format proved hugely controversial - several Games veterans and 2018 podium finishers were eliminated before the weekend crowds arrived - and it was abandoned within two years.

events.name: First Cut
events.description:
4 rounds for time:
400-m run
3 legless rope climbs
7 squat snatches (185 lb men / 130 lb women)

Time cap: 20 minutes.
The opening event of the Games; only the top 75 athletes in each division advanced to Event 2.
events.notes: Contested in the outdoor North Park stadium. The 12 total legless rope climbs inside the 20-minute cap proved the decisive element. Nearly half the field (everyone below 75th) was eliminated immediately, including several Games veterans, igniting the format controversy that defined 2019.

events.name: Second Cut
events.description:
For time:
800-m row
66 kettlebell shoulder-to-overheads (two 16-kg/35-lb kettlebells men, two 12-kg/26-lb kettlebells women)
132-ft handstand walk

Standards: the kettlebells had to pass below the chin between reps; the handstand walk was completed in 44-ft sections, and athletes had to restart from the last completed section if they came down.
Time cap: 10 minutes. Top 50 advanced.
events.notes: Rookie Danielle Brandon took a breakout event win over the women's field. The light kettlebells made cycling speed and the below-the-chin standard, not strength, the test. Field cut from 75 to 50 after this event.

events.name: Ruck
events.description:
6,000-m ruck run for time:
4 laps of a 1,500-m course wearing a rucksack, adding weight each lap: 20 lb, then 30 lb, then 40 lb, then 50 lb (same loading for men and women).

Time cap: 40 minutes. Top 40 advanced.
events.notes: Friday's 10 a.m. opener, run on a 1,500-m loop around the Alliant Energy Center grounds starting from North Park. First weighted ruck run contested at the Games. Sweden's Lukas Högberg beat Joshua Wichtrup by about 20 seconds; Emily Rolfe edged Tia-Clair Toomey by about 2 seconds for her first career event win. Field cut from 50 to 40.

events.name: Sprint Couplet
events.description:
For time:
172-ft sled push
18 bar muscle-ups (men) / 15 bar muscle-ups (women)
172-ft sled push

Time cap: 6 minutes. Top 30 advanced.
Sled weight was not published by CrossFit (fixed competition sleds, same implement for the whole division).
events.notes: Contested in heats in North Park. Matt McLeod beat Noah Ohlsen by 1.1 seconds; Amanda Barnhart overhauled Jamie Greene on the final sled push. All finishers were well under the cap. The sled load was never published on the official workout page. Field cut from 40 to 30.

events.name: Mary
events.description:
AMRAP 20 minutes:
5 handstand push-ups
10 alternating single-leg squats (pistols)
15 pull-ups

Score is total reps completed. Top 20 advanced.
events.notes: The classic bodyweight benchmark Mary, contested Friday night in the Coliseum - its first appearance as a Games event. Noah Ohlsen won with a sprint finish over Mat Fraser to take the overall lead; Kari Pearce's 695 reps (23 rounds plus 5 HSPU) was the best score of either division. Field cut from 30 to 20.

events.name: Sprint
events.description:
Head-to-head zigzag sprint, run as a 3-round bracketed tournament in heats of 5 on a multi-turn zigzag course on the North Park field.
Round 1: 4 heats of 5 (the 20 remaining athletes).
Round 2: 2 heats of 5.
Final: 1 heat of 5.
Scoring: places 1-5 awarded by finishing order in the final round; places 6-10 by second-round times; places 11-20 by first-round times.
Exact course length was not published. Top 10 advanced to the final day.
events.notes: Officially titled 'Sprint'; CrossFit's own event-summary videos call it the ZigZag Sprint. The cut to 10 after this event eliminated 13 Games veterans, including three 2018 podium finishers, and was the most criticized moment of the cut format. Leaderboard displays the winners' scores as 20 points from the bracket's internal scoring table.

events.name: Split Triplet
events.description:
5 rounds for time:
1 pegboard ascent
100 double-unders
10 single-arm dumbbell hang split snatches (80 lb men / 55 lb women)
10 single-arm dumbbell hang clean and split jerks (80 lb men / 55 lb women)

Standards: arms alternate on the hang dumbbell movements; the lead leg in the split must be opposite the working arm.
Time cap: 20 minutes.
movements: Single-Arm Dumbbell Hang Clean and Split Jerk
events.notes: First event of the Saturday night Coliseum session for the final 10. Fraser's win, with overall leader Ohlsen just behind, began his decisive surge. The split-footwork dumbbell lifts (single-arm hang split snatch, hang clean and split jerk) were widely treated as new tests, but no authoritative source confirms they were first-time Games movements, so firstAtGames is null (unknown) rather than asserting the debut; the dumbbell as an implement debuted earlier.

events.name: Clean
events.description:
1-rep-max clean ladder.
Men's published bars: 315-325-335-345-355-365-370-375-380-385 lb.
Women's published bars: 215-220-225-230-235-240-245-250-255-260 lb.
The final 10 athletes lifted in reverse order of the overall standings, advancing bar to bar; failing a bar ended the athlete's ladder. Athletes who failed were separated by a 5-rep-for-time tiebreak at 295 lb (men) / 195 lb (women).
Score is the heaviest successful clean.
events.notes: Saturday night Coliseum closer. Source conflict: the official workout page's published women's ladder tops out at 260 lb, but the official leaderboard and contemporaneous recaps record Toomey's winning lift at 265 lb, so the floor loading extended past the published progression. Fraser's 380-lb clean gave him back-to-back wins on the night and the overall lead he carried into Sunday.

events.name: Swim Paddle
events.description:
For time:
1,000-m swim
1,000-m paddle

Athletes swam a 1,000-m buoy circuit in Lake Monona, returned to shore, then paddled a board over the same 1,000-m course.
Time cap: 50 minutes.
events.notes: Sunday morning offsite event at Lake Monona, contested by only the final 10 per division. McLeod's second event win of the week; Toomey's winning time was within a tenth of a second of McLeod's.

events.name: Ringer 1
events.description:
For time:
30-cal Echo bike, 30 toes-to-rings
20-cal Echo bike, 20 toes-to-rings
10-cal Echo bike, 10 toes-to-rings

Time cap: 6 minutes (men) / 7 minutes (women). Scored separately from Ringer 2, which began 1 minute after the Ringer 1 time cap.
events.notes: First of the back-to-back 'Ringer' couplets in the Coliseum on Sunday afternoon. Time cap differed by division (6 min men / 7 min women, per the official workout page, which lists 'Time cap: 7 (W) / 6 (M) minutes'); a single numeric timeCapMin cannot represent both divisions, so it is null - see description for both caps. Toes-to-rings is believed to be a first-time Games movement, but no authoritative source confirms the debut, so firstAtGames is null (unknown) rather than asserting it.

events.name: Ringer 2
events.description:
For time:
15 burpees to ring touch, 15 overhead squats (135 lb men / 95 lb women)
10 burpees to ring touch, 10 overhead squats
5 burpees to ring touch, 5 overhead squats

Began exactly 1 minute after the Ringer 1 time cap, on the same floor. Time cap: 5 minutes.
events.notes: Scored separately from Ringer 1 despite running on a continuous clock (men started at 7:00, women at 8:00 of the combined window). Source conflict: Wikipedia describes a 6-minute cap starting 7 minutes after Ringer 1 began; the official workout page says a 5-minute cap beginning 1 minute after the Ringer 1 cap - the official version is recorded here. Davíðsdóttir swept both Ringers.

events.name: The Standard
events.description:
For time:
30 clean and jerks (135 lb men / 95 lb women)
30 ring muscle-ups
30 snatches (135 lb men / 95 lb women)

The opening 30 clean and jerks are the benchmark 'Grace' and the closing 30 snatches are the benchmark 'Isabel', separated by 30 ring muscle-ups.
Time cap: 12 minutes.
events.notes: Final event, Sunday evening in the Coliseum. Both champions won the event outright: Fraser sealed his fourth straight title (tying Rich Froning), and Toomey her third straight, the first woman to do so. Combines the benchmarks Grace and Isabel but is not itself a named benchmark.
